name: One signature, bought with a near-black ground
premise: The current kit correctly proves no single accent clears 4.5:1 against both white and its Ink (#0B0E14): the arithmetic window (L <= 0.1833 on paper, L >= 0.1946 on ink) is empty for any one value. Solve for the ground instead of the accent: at a ground luminance <= ~0.0019 (roughly #050608 or darker), the window opens, L in [0.175, 0.18333] -- narrow, but real. This direction buys back a single true signature colour across both themes, and pays for it in a ground that reads as OLED-black rather than a brand-tinted indigo. The engine below must re-derive this window to four decimal places -- the arithmetic above is a hypothesis, not a given.

ground.label: Undertow
ground.note: Near-black, chosen to open the single-signature contrast window, not for its own sake.

accent_light.label: Meridian ember (light)
accent_light.note: Provisional single-value anchor -- the engine solves the true achievable value; this is a starting hue only.

accent_dark.label: Meridian ember (dark)
accent_dark.note: Same anchor as accent_light on purpose -- the whole premise of this direction is ONE value in both themes. The engine proves whether this single value actually clears both grounds.

support.label: Ash
support.note: A warm neutral, doing the job Ember did in D1 -- support without adding a second chromatic family.
